reasoning_traces.think:
The unit economics model operates as a vector space where revenue streams and cost components define basis vectors. Revenue types map to orthogonal dimensions in a payoff tensor, enabling linear decomposition of total financial performance. Cost structure acts as a kernel that modulates these revenues through fixed and variable cost functions. Key metrics like LTV/CAC, margin, and payback period emerge as scalar projections onto this space. Dualities arise in the relationship between acquisition efficiency and retention rates—where high CAC must be offset by long-term LTV. Failure modes include negative margins due to cost overrun or insufficient revenue scaling. The system exhibits nonlinearity when churn accelerates beyond break-even thresholds. Each primitive supports a layered state transition in GSE, where financial health drives strategic decisions.
